before_times: What needs cleaning: the air ducts, the dryer vent, or both
Air ducts: how many heating and cooling systems, how many vents and returns, and about how many square feet
Dryer vent: electric or gas dryer, how long the run is, how many floors, and whether it exits through the wall or the roof
When the ducts or the dryer vent were last cleaned
Signs of trouble: clothes taking two cycles to dry, a very hot laundry room, lint outside, dust blowing from the vents
A home built before 1980, or ducts wrapped in old insulation (an asbestos check comes first)
Any animals heard in the ducts or the vent
At the counter: which items, and what they're made of
after_time: Who will be home: the customer, or someone else (their name and mobile go on the secure page)
Where the furnace or air handler is, and the attic or crawl space access
Where the dryer vent comes out, and parking
Own or rent: the landlord's OK for anything beyond cleaning
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns or rents the home, or someone the owner allows. A renter books cleaning; the landlord's OK is needed for anything beyond cleaning.

stop: smoke or flames from a dryer, a vent, a furnace or the ducts
a gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm
suspected asbestos on ducts or pipes
a mold patch over the state's size cutoff
dead animals or heavy droppings in the ducts
an attic or crawl space floor that isn't safe
safety_and_stop_words.go_on: Yes, with the part left out (asbestos, mold, droppings, sewage, wiring, a floor), and for signs of a clogged dryer vent. No, for smoke or flames now, a gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm.
stop_action: Smoke or flames now: get everyone out of the house, then call 911 from outside. Rosie never places the call. No booking until the fire department clears it.
A gas smell or a carbon monoxide alarm: get everyone outside now, then call 911 and the gas company. No booking until it's safe.

Signs of a clogged dryer vent (clothes damp after a full cycle, a very hot dryer or laundry room, lint at the outside vent) are not an emergency: stop using the dryer until the vent is cleaned. The booking goes on.

Suspected asbestos, mold over the cutoff, droppings, sewage: Rosie says a duct cleaner can't take that part on and points to a specialist. The rest of the home can still be booked with that part left out.
Sparking wires or an unsafe attic floor: stay out of the area; no booking for it until it's fixed.
Animals heard in the ducts or the vent: a wildlife company first. Protected birds nesting in an outside vent stay until they leave; no cleaning or cap removal until then.

prep: Clear about 3 feet around the vents, the furnace and the dryer
Move small items and rugs off the floor vents
At the counter: bring the filters dry, with their frames

skills: Air duct cleaning with negative pressure (a crew of two)
Dryer vent cleaning, including roof exits
Counter work: degreasing filters, registers, vent covers and lint trap screens
staff.licenses_or_certificates: None per person unless the state's form says so. A trade group's certificate shows only as the person gave it, not checked.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs fees, walkthrough quotes, repairs over the limit and same-day jobs. The office manager may OK prices if the owner sets it.
staff.stand_in: Another crew lead with the same skill, at the same window and price.
staff.crews: Two per whole-home duct job: a lead, who holds the entry code and texts DONE, and a helper. A person who works alone (a dryer vent technician) adds an emergency contact, and a missed safety check gives that contact the job's address only.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult who owns or rents the home, or someone the owner allows. A renter books cleaning; the landlord's OK is needed for anything beyond cleaning.

visit.check_in: The check-in code at the door, entered by the crew lead. The on-my-way text names the crew lead, with a photo.
visit.done: DONE with the bill's lines and the after photos or the camera video. The report goes with the receipt.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Cleaning air ducts and dryer vents needs no state license in most places. Where a state or city licenses home improvement or HVAC work, its form asks for it. Cutting, sealing or repairing ducts, replacing a dryer vent, and gas or electric work can need an HVAC or contractor license, or a gas fitter's license, where the state requires one; this business cleans only. Asbestos removal and mold removal over the state's size cutoff are separate licensed trades and are not offered. The vent shop's counter: business registration only.
license.who: The business. Crew members and shop techs need no license of their own unless the state's form says so.
license.ask: The company's business registration, or its contractor or HVAC license, where the state's form asks for one.
license.insurance: General liability and workers' comp are common. 'Insured' is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
license.background: Crews work inside homes: the business's own word that they are checked, or a check Rosie holds where the state's rules require one. It is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
